listenbrainz.note: Train graph excludes all events after train cutoff; validation/test are later days, capped at first 500 eligible users.

onion.note: 90% users train; 10% held out, deterministic profile/target partition; aggregate data has no temporal claim.

yambda.scope: Anonymous source-local confidence calibration; IDs/embeddings are not mapped to named songs or shipped.

retained_metadata.scope: Prior CC0 metadata coverage only; no old graph, held-out events or popularity weights reused.

wikidata.scope: Artist genre context through exact artist MBIDs; no inferred song language.

onion_acoustic.algorithm: standardised, L2 normalised, two deterministic hyperplane tables; bounded cosine neighbours

fma_acoustic.algorithm: standardised, L2 normalised, two deterministic hyperplane tables; bounded cosine neighbours

discogs.scope: Release context only, no verified cross-source recording joins.

openopus.scope: Conservative composition context, never a playable recording ID.

compression_fidelity.scope: Agreement with trained graph neighbours versus random records; not next-song accuracy.

algorithm: Three-step graph diffusion, source-identity duplicate weighting, hashed 32D embeddings, int8 quantisation
limitations: Hash collisions and quantisation trade precision for size.
The full named catalogue is not bundled: the small vocabulary adds limited discoveries, and live provider radio/search supplies current candidates.
No claim that all 583k source records are unique songs, or locally searchable names.
Streaming and resolving new playback IDs still need the provider; raw listening histories stay in training storage.
